sections.heading: D — Accuracy and verification
sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy and verification

Source: every knowledge fact in parts C and C2 cites exactly one physical page of the private snapshot of the Washington Driver Guide, the issuer's own publication, read from extracted page text.
Confidence: high for the failure, collision, power line and traffic stop facts, each restated from one explicit list item or numbered step; nothing was taken from memory or from a non-issuer source.
Precision rule: the flare placement range, the collision report deadline, the power line distance and the ticket response window are kept exactly as printed inside cited fact blocks in C and C2, with the wording paraphrased so that no learner line copies the guide.
Accuracy flags: one fact in C places the court route and the supervisor request in a single sentence about disagreeing with an officer, but the guide ties the supervisor request to concerns about the officer's conduct; the confusable block in C2 states the distinction correctly and should be preferred (verify — sec14-D-FLAG).
Stability: the guide is a single published revision and states it may lag new legislation, so any rule that a future law changes must be re-read from the current edition before reuse.
External review: none requested; the first aid, power line and police stop lines restate only the guide's own printed guidance for exam preparation and add no medical or legal advice beyond it.

corpus_stability.reason: The Washington Driver Guide is one published guide revision (form line 520-400 R/4/25 on physical p4); the guide itself notes it may lag recent legislative changes, and nothing on the selected pages indicates more than one rewrite per year.

verification_debt.claim_text: sec14-F37 (physical p182) frames requesting a supervisor as a response to disagreement; the guide ties it to believing the officer acted inappropriately or questions about conduct. sec14-R09 states it correctly; F37 should be re-authored in a later pass
